# mirtverse

**mirtverse** is a friendly workflow and reporting layer for the
[mirt](https://philchalmers.github.io/mirt/) package. mirt estimates
item response theory (IRT) models; mirtverse helps you choose a model,
understand the results, make publication-ready figures, and share
everything, with or without writing R code.

> **New: interactive teaching labs.** Six browser-based labs let
> students fit live mirt models and make real testing decisions, from
> choosing a model to advising a certification board, investigating a
> fairness complaint, linking two forms of an exam, designing an
> adaptive test and checking rater-scored open-ended responses. Start
> one with `run_lab("model-choice")`, or read [Teaching
> labs](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/teaching-labs.html).

## About mirt

[mirt](https://philchalmers.github.io/mirt/), developed and maintained
by [Dr. R. Philip Chalmers](https://chalmers.info.yorku.ca/), is one of
the most comprehensive open-source packages for item response theory. It
was introduced in the *Journal of Statistical Software* ([Chalmers,
2012](https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v048.i06)) and has been developed
continuously since, with version 1.48 released on CRAN in October 2026.
It is widely used in research on educational and psychological
measurement.

mirt can:

- **Estimate a wide range of models:** unidimensional and
  multidimensional, exploratory and confirmatory, bifactor and two-tier,
  with more than 30 item types (Rasch, 2PL to 4PL, graded response,
  (generalized) partial credit, nominal, ideal-point, nonparametric
  spline items and more), plus user-defined items.
- **Handle complex designs:** multiple-group analysis and measurement
  invariance, mixed-effects and explanatory IRT
  ([`mixedmirt()`](https://philchalmers.github.io/mirt/reference/mixedmirt.html)),
  and latent class and diagnostic classification models
  ([`mdirt()`](https://philchalmers.github.io/mirt/reference/mdirt.html)).
- **Use several estimation engines:** EM with fixed or quasi-Monte Carlo
  quadrature, and the Metropolis-Hastings Robbins-Monro (MHRM) algorithm
  for high-dimensional models, with several standard-error methods.
- **Check and use the models:** item and person fit, limited-information
  fit (M2), local dependence, DIF and differential test functioning, and
  ability estimation (EAP, MAP, ML, WLE, plausible values).

mirtverse leaves all of this untouched and adds the workflow,
interpretation and reporting tools around it.

## What mirtverse adds

| Feature | Functions |
|----|----|
| Point-and-click workbench with R code export | [`launch_workbench()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/launch_workbench.md) |
| Analysis scripts written from a plain-language request | [`mv_ask()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_ask.md), [`mv_ask_setup()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_ask_setup.md), [`run_script()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/run_script.md) |
| Model selection assistant | [`select_model()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/select_model.md) |
| Differential item functioning in one call | [`dif()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/dif.md), [`gg_dif()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_dif.md) |
| Plain-language interpretation | [`interpret()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/interpret.md), [`interpret_prompt()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/interpret_prompt.md) |
| Tidy outputs | [`tidy()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/tidy.html), [`glance()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/glance.html), [`augment()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/augment.html), [`item_table()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/item_table.md) |
| ggplot2 graphics, including Wright maps | [`gg_trace()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_trace.md), [`gg_info()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_info.md), [`gg_wright()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_wright.md), [`gg_itemfit()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_itemfit.md), [`gg_q3()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_q3.md), [`gg_scores()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_scores.md), [`gg_empirical()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_empirical.md), [`autoplot()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/autoplot.html) |
| Item health cards | [`item_card()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/item_card.md), [`item_cards()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/item_cards.md) |
| One-call HTML report | [`mv_report()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_report.md) |
| Results dashboard to share with non-R users, as a Shiny app or one offline HTML file | [`mv_dashboard()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_dashboard.md), [`export_dashboard()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/export_dashboard.md) |
| Response-time modelling and rapid-guessing detection | [`fit_rt()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/fit_rt.md), [`sim_rt()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/sim_rt.md) |
| Interactive teaching labs for measurement courses (learnr) | [`run_lab()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/run_lab.md), [`list_labs()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/run_lab.md) |
| Translate ltm, eRm, TAM and irtQ code into mirt code | [`mirtify()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mirtify.md), [`mirtify_crosswalk()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mirtify_crosswalk.md) |

## Installation

Install a prebuilt version from r-universe (no Rtools or GitHub token
needed):

``` r

install.packages("mirtverse", repos = c("https://okanbulut.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
```

Or install the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("okanbulut/mirtverse")
```

## A five-minute tour

``` r

library(mirtverse)

data <- expand.table(LSAT7)

sel <- select_model(data)   # compares Rasch, 2PL and 3PL and recommends one
mod <- sel$best             # an ordinary mirt model

interpret(mod)              # what the results mean, in plain language
tidy(mod)                   # parameters as a data frame
item_table(mod)             # item statistics, fit and flags in one table

gg_wright(mod)              # person-item map
item_card(mod, "Item.2")    # one-page item review

mv_report(sel, file = "report.html")   # everything in one HTML file
mv_dashboard(mod, title = "LSAT results")   # interactive dashboard to share
```

Prefer clicking? Run
[`launch_workbench()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/launch_workbench.md).
Prefer describing the analysis in words?
`mv_ask("fit a 2PL, check DIF by gender and make a report", data = mydata)`
writes the whole script for you.

Teaching a measurement course? `run_lab("model-choice")` opens an
interactive lab in which students work through a realistic testing
scenario with live models (see [Teaching
labs](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/teaching-labs.html)).

## Coming from ltm, eRm, TAM or irtQ?

[`mirtify()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mirtify.md)
rewrites code written for these packages as mirt code, without running
the original, and adds a comment wherever the packages differ (for
example, conditional versus marginal likelihood in eRm, or the scaling
constant `D = 1.702` in irtQ):

``` r

mirtify({
  library(eRm)
  fit <- RM(raschdat1)
  pp <- person.parameter(fit)
  itemfit(pp)
  LRtest(fit)
})
```

It translates the model calls and the usual next steps (scores, item and
person fit, plots, Andersen’s LR test), and `run = TRUE` also runs the
result. In the package tests, most translated models reproduce the
original estimates to within about 0.006.
[`mirtify_crosswalk()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mirtify_crosswalk.md)
lists every supported function. See [Moving from ltm, eRm, TAM or irtQ
to mirt](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/mirtify.html).

## Relationship to mirt

**mirtverse depends on mirt and never changes how models are
estimated**. Every function accepts a model created with
[`mirt::mirt()`](https://philchalmers.github.io/mirt/reference/mirt.html),
so you can move between the two packages at any point. Please cite mirt
(Chalmers, 2012) whenever you use mirtverse.

Chalmers, R. P. (2012). mirt: A multidimensional item response theory
package for the R environment. *Journal of Statistical Software, 48*(6),
1-29. <https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v048.i06>

## Citation

If you use mirtverse, please cite it together with mirt. Run
`citation("mirtverse")` in R, or use:

Bulut, O. (2026). *mirtverse: A friendly workflow and reporting layer
for ‘mirt’* (Version 0.2.0) \[R package\]. Zenodo.
<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23836292>

To cite all versions, use <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23719384>,
which always resolves to the latest release.

# Package index

## Workbench

Point-and-click analysis with reproducible code.

- [`launch_workbench()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/launch_workbench.md)
  [`workbench_app()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/launch_workbench.md)
  : Launch the mirtverse workbench

## Scripts from plain language

Describe an analysis in words and get a complete, tested R script.

- [`mv_ask()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_ask.md)
  : Write an analysis script from a plain-language request
- [`mv_ask_setup()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_ask_setup.md)
  : Set up an AI model for mv_ask()
- [`mv_plan()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_plan.md)
  [`update_plan()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_plan.md)
  : An analysis plan for mv_ask()
- [`run_script()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/run_script.md)
  [`save_script()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/run_script.md)
  : Run or save a script written by mv_ask()
- [`profile_data()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/profile_data.md)
  : Summarise a data set without revealing its values

## Coming from other IRT packages

Translate ltm, eRm, TAM and irtQ code into mirt code.

- [`mirtify()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mirtify.md)
  : Translate ltm, eRm, TAM and irtQ code into mirt code
- [`mirtify_crosswalk()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mirtify_crosswalk.md)
  : The ltm, eRm, TAM and irtQ to mirt crosswalk

## Assessment pipeline

Take a test from response data to a technical report in stages, with
checks and flags to consider before each next stage.

- [`mv_pipeline()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_pipeline.md)
  [`tidy(`*`<mv_pipeline>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_pipeline.md)
  : Start an assessment pipeline
- [`set_blueprint()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/set_blueprint.md)
  : Pipeline stage: test blueprint and construct definition
- [`generate_items()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/generate_items.md)
  [`add_items()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/generate_items.md)
  [`verify_items()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/generate_items.md)
  : Pipeline stage: item generation
- [`review_packet()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/review_packet.md)
  [`read_reviews()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/review_packet.md)
  : Pipeline stage: item review
- [`design_field_test()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/design_field_test.md)
  : Pipeline stage: field-test design
- [`add_responses()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/add_responses.md)
  : Pipeline stage: data intake and cleaning
- [`calibrate()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/calibrate.md)
  : Pipeline stage: calibration
- [`link_to_bank()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/link_to_bank.md)
  : Pipeline stage: link a calibration to an item bank
- [`bank_items()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/bank_items.md)
  : Pipeline stage: add items to a bank
- [`mv_bank()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_bank.md)
  [`tidy(`*`<mv_bank>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_bank.md)
  : An item bank
- [`assemble_forms()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/assemble_forms.md)
  : Pipeline stage: assemble fixed test forms
- [`simulate_cat()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/simulate_cat.md)
  : Pipeline stage: simulate a computerized adaptive test
- [`assemble_mst()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/assemble_mst.md)
  : Pipeline stage: assemble and simulate a multistage test
- [`set_cuts()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/set_cuts.md)
  : Pipeline stage: cut scores and decision quality
- [`item_map()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/item_map.md)
  : Item map for Bookmark standard setting
- [`score_open()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/score_open.md)
  : Pipeline stage: scoring open-ended responses
- [`score_persons()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/score_persons.md)
  : Pipeline stage: score test takers
- [`check_security()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/check_security.md)
  : Pipeline stage: test security
- [`pipeline_report()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/pipeline_report.md)
  : Pipeline stage: technical report
- [`monitor_bank()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/monitor_bank.md)
  : Pipeline stage: bank monitoring
- [`retire_items()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/retire_items.md)
  : Retire bank items or send them back to review
- [`flags()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/flags.md) :
  List the flags raised by a pipeline
- [`acknowledge()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/acknowledge.md)
  [`override()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/acknowledge.md)
  : Record a decision about a flag
- [`drop_items()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/drop_items.md)
  : Remove items from a pipeline
- [`mv_rules()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_rules.md)
  : Thresholds for the pipeline checks

## Choosing and understanding a model

- [`select_model()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/select_model.md)
  : Model selection assistant
- [`interpret()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/interpret.md)
  : Plain-language interpretation of IRT results
- [`interpret_prompt()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/interpret_prompt.md)
  : Build a prompt for an AI assistant from a fitted model

## Tidy outputs

- [`tidy(`*`<SingleGroupClass>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/tidy_mirt.md)
  [`tidy(`*`<MultipleGroupClass>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/tidy_mirt.md)
  : Tidy a mirt model into a data frame of parameters
- [`glance(`*`<SingleGroupClass>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/glance_mirt.md)
  [`glance(`*`<MultipleGroupClass>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/glance_mirt.md)
  : One-row model summary
- [`augment(`*`<SingleGroupClass>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/augment_mirt.md)
  : Add person scores to the response data
- [`item_table()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/item_table.md)
  : Tidy item statistics and item fit in one table

## Graphics

- [`gg_dif()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_dif.md)
  : DIF effect sizes plot
- [`gg_empirical()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_empirical.md)
  : Empirical versus model-implied item curve
- [`gg_info()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_info.md)
  : Test and item information curves
- [`gg_itemfit()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_itemfit.md)
  : Item fit plot
- [`gg_q3()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_q3.md) :
  Local dependence heatmap (Yen's Q3)
- [`gg_scores()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_scores.md)
  : Distribution of person scores
- [`gg_trace()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_trace.md)
  : Item characteristic (trace) curves
- [`gg_wright()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_wright.md)
  : Wright map (person-item map)
- [`autoplot(`*`<SingleGroupClass>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/autoplot.SingleGroupClass.md)
  : Plot a mirt model with ggplot2
- [`theme_mirtverse()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/theme_mirtverse.md)
  : A clean ggplot2 theme for psychometric graphics

# Articles

### Guides

- [Getting started with
  mirtverse](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/mirtverse.md):

- [The mirtverse
  workbench](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/workbench.md):

- [Response times and rapid
  guessing](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/response-times.md):

- [mv_ask(): from a sentence to a tested R
  script](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/mv-ask-guide.md):

  How mv_ask() turns a plain-language request into a complete IRT
  analysis script, with worked examples and benchmark results for
  Claude, GPT and local Ollama models.

- [Sharing results with a
  dashboard](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/dashboards.md):

  Turn a fitted model into an interactive dashboard for people who do
  not use R, and share it as a single HTML file or a Shiny app.

- [Moving from ltm, eRm, TAM or irtQ to
  mirt](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/mirtify.md):

  Translate existing IRT code into mirt with mirtify(), see what changes
  and why, and look up any function in the crosswalk.

- [An assessment pipeline from blueprint to bank
  monitoring](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/assessment-pipeline.md):

  Take a certification exam through every stage of the mirtverse
  assessment pipeline, with the checks and decisions at each step.

### Teaching and learning

- [Teaching labs for measurement
  courses](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/teaching-labs.md):

  Interactive learnr labs in which students fit live mirt models and
  make the decisions a psychometrician makes, from scoring and model
  choice to interpretation and fairness. Includes an instructor guide
  and answer key.

- [A course map for
  instructors](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/course-map.md):

  A suggested 12-week syllabus for a university course in item response
  theory, linking each week to mirtverse articles, labs, functions and
  datasets.

- [Glossary of IRT
  terms](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/glossary.md):

  Plain-language definitions of the terms used in item response theory,
  each with the mirtverse or mirt function that computes it, and
  pictures where a picture helps.
